---
name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: AyushRajSinghParihar
  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines
---

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platforms: iOS/tvOS/visionOS where available. Joining automatically broadcasts the person’s microphone, a late join restarts playback for everyone and leaving ends every participant’s session without warning. Some people lack content access.

# Apple HIG: Integrate a capability into the product task

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the product benefit and capability prerequisites before entering the technology-specific procedure. Avoid adding a system integration solely to decorate an existing flow.
2. Define consent/account/capability availability and the meaningful result, cancel, failure and recovery paths applicable to that integration. Keep sensitive information and system ownership clear.
3. Preserve supplied branding, hardware and platform qualifications. HIG states experience expectations; verify current APIs against implementation documentation when writing framework-specific code.
4. Deliver an integration contract or correction in the existing stack, with source-supported choices, fallbacks and evidence limits. Do not claim a payment, health, spatial or connected-device runtime test from a static specimen.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

# Apple HIG: Platform and task adaptation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the person’s primary task and the target platform before translating a screen. Read that platform’s procedure; use Principles to resolve hierarchy and Designing for games only for gameplay.
2. Compare navigation, window/scene model, primary input, attention duration and state restoration. Preserve the product task while changing the interaction appropriate to the destination platform.
3. For device changes such as opening an iPhone Duo or resizing an iPad window, specify what selection, editing state and route survive each transition.
4. Deliver a platform-decision matrix or an adaptation patch, with concrete acceptance scenarios for each materially different interaction.

# Apple HIG: Perception, meaning and adaptable presentation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the actual barrier or design decision: readability, visual hierarchy, imagery meaning, movement, locale, privacy or spatial placement. Choose the corresponding topic procedure rather than loading every foundation.
2. For text access, combine Typography with Accessibility only where size, reflow or reading alternatives matter. Use VoiceOver when grouping, semantics or navigation needs a procedure of its own.
3. For color/material decisions, separate content hierarchy from controls and evaluate the actual appearance/background/settings context. Preserve semantic meaning when appearance changes.
4. Deliver prioritized evidence-backed corrections or a concrete presentation specification. Distinguish inspected contrast/layout evidence from runtime and assistive-technology checks still needed.

name: apple-hig-designing-for-ios
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting an iPhone experience for handheld touch, interrupted use, orientation changes, and system entrypoints.
---

# Make the iPhone task usable in the hand

Read [Designing for iOS](../../references/designing-for-ios.md). Inspect the current task, its entry and return points, supported orientations, input, and any supplied implementation. Distinguish a brief check from extended work. For a review, anchor problems to supplied screens/behavior; for design or adaptation, revise the requested artifact in its existing stack.

Choose what must remain immediately visible during the task. A brief check needs its result and primary action close together; extended editing can expose additional controls without crowding the initial screen. Put frequent touch actions within comfortable reach, generally toward the middle/lower display, while preserving system navigation and swipe-back behavior. Move secondary commands into a short discoverable path rather than shrinking every control to fit.

Trace interruption and resumption: preserve the selected item, draft, or playback context when another app takes focus. Specify portrait/landscape and enlarged-text rearrangements without inventing a new navigation hierarchy for each orientation. Use touch and onscreen keyboard as the baseline, then offer appropriate voice or accessory paths. Add location, biometric, payment, or motion features only when their benefit reduces task effort and access is appropriate.

For repeated out-of-app actions, choose a relevant system entrypoint and a precise destination: a quick action starts an action, search opens the found content, and a widget exposes a useful glance. Do not add every entrypoint to every app.

**Before → decision → after:** A parcel app opens a dense desktop-style table and requires opening three menus to find the latest delivery. A handheld glance needs delivery state first. The revised home screen shows the active parcel and “Show pickup code,” keeps history one step away, and returns a widget tap to that parcel rather than a generic home screen.

Deliver a revised screen/flow or implementation plus interruption, orientation, and text-size acceptance checks. Fail if the primary action becomes unreachable, Back conflicts with a custom gesture, or resuming loses work. Screenshot review cannot establish touch comfort or actual system integration; state pending device checks.

For detailed adaptation use [Layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md); for custom touch gestures use [Gestures](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-gestures/SKILL.md); for a chosen glance use [Widgets](../../../apple-hig-system-experiences/.topics/apple-hig-widgets/SKILL.md).

---
name: apple-hig-designing-for-tvos
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting an Apple TV experience for across-room viewing, remote focus navigation, shared viewers, or television discovery.
---

# Make television choices visible from across the room

Read [Designing for tvOS](../../references/designing-for-tvos.md). Inspect the primary activity, content hierarchy, viewer/profile model, authentication, and input assumptions. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode and use supplied evidence to separate confirmed defects from untested remote behavior.

Rebuild the hierarchy around distant viewing and focus navigation. Prioritize legible titles and recognizable imagery rather than filling the TV with desktop density. Map directional movement and selection from each major region. The focused item must visibly identify both location and the available action through the platform's focus treatment; do not leave essential navigation dependent on pointer hover or tiny touch targets.

Choose the appropriate input contract. Siri Remote must support ordinary browsing; games may add controllers and relevant companion/voice input. Avoid making controller possession necessary for non-controller tasks. For long sessions or picture-in-picture, preserve the person's place when attention changes.

Reduce repetitive authentication using appropriate system integration. If the current system viewer changes, switch to the matching app profile deliberately and preserve privacy boundaries. Add Top Shelf, TV-app discovery, provider support, or SharePlay only when the content/activity warrants it, with a destination that matches the selected item.

**Before → decision → after:** A cooking-video app uses small tab labels, pointer hover menus, and one permanently signed-in household profile. Decision: across-room remote browsing and changing viewers require explicit focus routes and profile ownership. After, clear focusable categories lead into large recipe artwork, Select starts the highlighted recipe, and a viewer change updates saved recipes instead of exposing another person's history.

Deliver a focus-route map and corrected screen/profile flow or implementation. Fail if focus is invisible, a region has no remote exit, or a viewer change retains another profile's personal content. Check actual remote traversal, television legibility, and focus enlargement on supported hardware; a desktop screenshot only supports visual hypotheses.

For detailed movement use [Focus and selection](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-focus-and-selection/SKILL.md) and [Remotes](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-remotes/SKILL.md); for shared viewing use [SharePlay](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-shareplay/SKILL.md).

---
name: apple-hig-designing-for-visionos
description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting an experience for Apple Vision Pro, including spatial presentation, Shared Space, Full Space, eye and hand interaction, or comfort.
---

# Choose a useful spatial experience

Read [Designing for visionOS](../../references/designing-for-visionos.md). Use it for platform principles; the task mapping and deliverable structure below are application engineering advice. Do not treat a desktop interface floated in space or full immersion everywhere as the default solution.

## Establish the task and evidence

Inspect the supplied product, screens, spatial storyboard, input model, or implementation. Identify the core activity, what genuinely benefits from depth or immersion, whether collaboration matters, and whether use is seated, standing, or movement-dependent. Distinguish design, review, and adaptation: produce the requested spatial design, evidence-backed findings, or revised artifact rather than a list of platform features. Preserve the existing product's useful content and state when adapting it.

Record what the evidence can establish. A flat mockup cannot establish depth comfort, reach, tracking, or indirect-target responsiveness. Resolve unspecified details with stated assumptions unless they change the purpose or physical requirements of the experience.

## Decide presentation per activity

Map each major task to a presentation and explain why the least immersive option meets or fails its needs:

- Use a standard **window** for contained tasks such as browsing, text entry, settings, and ordinary controls. Allow people to position it; preserve readability through the platform's dynamic scaling rather than baking a fixed viewing distance into the design.
- Use a **volume or spatial object** when inspecting a genuinely three-dimensional subject benefits the task. Identify what stays in a window, how the object is selected/manipulated, and how the person returns to the rest of the work. A 3D object alone does not justify replacing the surroundings.
- Choose **Full Space** for a specific valuable moment that needs an app-controlled spatial setting. Describe whether it retains surroundings, uses a portal, or surrounds the person. Specify deliberate entry and return, a stable visual reference, and how task state survives the transition. Read the immersive-experiences procedure before choosing detailed styles, boundaries, or transitions. Keep ordinary tasks in Shared Space where they work well.

Make system agency explicit: passthrough represents the real surroundings; the Digital Crown gives the person control over immersion. Do not design around preventing that control. If room understanding improves the experience, identify its user benefit and permission boundary rather than assuming access. Use Spatial Audio to convey useful spatial relationships, and consider SharePlay/spatial Personas only when a shared activity benefits from presence.

## Make the interaction physically sustainable

Choose the resting interaction first. Eye targeting plus indirect hand activation must work with hands in the lap or at the sides. Use direct manipulation for nearby, brief interactions; provide another way to complete sustained work instead of requiring raised arms or repeated reach. Standard components offer an accessible starting point; describe equivalent navigation and activation for custom spatial content with the platform's assistive methods.

Place important content within comfortable view for different heights and postures. In full immersion, bring useful content to the resting person rather than requiring turns or body repositioning. Remove abrupt, overwhelming, or unsupported camera movement; provide stable references. Use the spatial-layout and accessibility procedures for detailed placement and accommodation. “Relative to the head” is a placement consideration, not permission to lock content rigidly to it.

If the intended scenario involves vehicles, heavy machinery, hazardous walking routes, or users younger than the source's 13+ device guidance, identify the conflict and revise the scenario. Consult the current Apple device user guide for operational restrictions rather than presenting this overview as a complete safety specification.

## Produce and verify a spatial artifact

Deliver a task-to-presentation map and a concrete revised storyboard, screen/scene specification, or implementation. Include entry/return behavior for immersive moments, resting and alternative input paths, and relevant comfort checks. For reviews, locate each issue in supplied evidence and show its corrected spatial behavior; mark unobserved behavior as needing verification.

Walk the complete task in each chosen presentation. Fail if ordinary work unnecessarily requires immersion, the person cannot return with context intact, essential controls demand repeated reach/turns, or motion lacks a stable reference. Inspect semantics and alternative actions where available. Validate reach, comfort, eye/hand targeting, posture variation, and assistive use in a worn Vision Pro environment before claiming those results. Linux artifact checks and simulator/static review can support narrower claims only; list device checks still pending.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** A pottery catalog proposes a fully surrounding showroom for choosing glaze, reading care notes, and inspecting a vase. Care notes float behind the person; rotating a vase requires sustained raised-hand dragging.

**Decision:** Inspection benefits from depth; reading and catalog selection do not require stronger immersion. Repeated direct manipulation would fatigue the person.

**After:** A movable Shared Space window holds catalog, glaze choices, and notes. A selected vase appears in a volume beside the relevant controls, with indirect rotation and reset actions usable with resting hands. An optional surrounding exhibit becomes a separately chosen moment with an explicit return preserving the selected vase. The storyboard annotates posture, targeting, and return-state tests; physical comfort remains unverified until device testing.

## Conditional handoffs

When a task needs Full Space, continue with [Immersive experiences](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-immersive-experiences/SKILL.md). For placement, scale, and depth use [Spatial layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md). For custom eye-targeted affordances use [Eyes](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-eyes/SKILL.md); for an assistive alternative use [Accessibility](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md). Use [SharePlay](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-shareplay/SKILL.md) only if the requested experience includes shared participation.

---
name: apple-hig-shareplay
description: Use when designing or reviewing synchronized SharePlay activities, invitation/join routes, entitlement prerequisites, shared versus personal state, or visionOS participant arrangements.
---

# Synchronize the activity while preserving each person's control

Read [SharePlay](../../references/shareplay.md). Inspect the simultaneous activity, content entitlements, join/leave paths, shared state, supported platforms, and requested design/review/adaptation. Preserve the existing stack. Watch is unsupported; later asynchronous collaboration needs saved state or links rather than SharePlay alone.

Choose which state is shared. Watching/browsing can use synchronized views; a game may need individual roles. Invite through recognizable controls/system sharing with concise accurate art/title/description. Bring joiners directly to the content, deferring nonessential profiles/onboarding and using dismissible necessary prerequisites. Account for each person's required purchased/subscribed entitlement instead of assuming the host grants access.

Explain who changed shared state and how a playback pause affects everyone. Retain per-person volume/subtitle/accessibility settings and a clear leave/rejoin route. Support phone/tablet Picture in Picture or a continuing Mac playback window where relevant.

For visionOS, distinguish ordinary window mirroring from volumes/immersive SharePlay. Keep shared objects/sound in consistent relative locations, handle simultaneous tools predictably, and ask before immersion changes interrupt other work. Choose side-by-side, surround, conversational, or custom seating by activity. Keep seats stable, sufficiently separated, and independent of player roles where possible; nearby real people cannot be virtually moved. Provide alternatives when gestures/facial expression or spatial Personas are unavailable.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a shared sculpture lesson forces every joiner through profile creation, steals another participant's tool on selection, and moves seats whenever someone leaves. Decision: participation needs direct entry and predictable shared context. After, required content access is clear, the lesson opens immediately after minimal prerequisites, tool ownership follows an explicit rule, and stable positions remain while people leave/rejoin.

Deliver join/shared-personal-state/leave contracts and spatial arrangements when applicable. Fail if joiners land generically, one person's accessibility preference is overwritten, tool collisions are unpredictable, or seat changes disorient. Actual synchronization, entitlements, FaceTime/Persona behavior, and multi-device comfort require supported participants/devices; static artifacts cannot verify them.

Use [Immersive experiences](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-immersive-experiences/SKILL.md) for immersion transitions and [Apple In-App Purchase](../apple-hig-apple-in-app-purchase/SKILL.md) for entitlement clarity.

description: Use when designing or reviewing permission timing, purpose strings, pre-permission explanations, tracking requests, data minimization, or private platform inputs.

# Ask for precise access when its purpose is clear

Read [Privacy](../../references/privacy.md). Inspect the feature's actual data needs, transfers, storage, current permission flow, and supported platform. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Produce the requested copy/flow/data-handling changes in the existing stack; distinguish documented platform restrictions from additional application recommendations.

Map each requested category to a specific feature and minimum necessary scope. Remove collection without a concrete benefit; prefer on-device work where it avoids unnecessary transfer. Explain collection/use accurately and flag App Store disclosure updates needed when behavior changes. Respect private email and tracking choices rather than designing around them.

Ask when the person invokes the feature. Launch-time requests need an essential, obvious dependency. Write a short active purpose sentence explaining use and reason. If context is sufficient, omit a custom pre-alert; if explanation is essential, use one clear continuation to the real system alert without imitating Allow/Don't Allow. Keep the guide's special pre-alert restrictions distinct from ordinary onboarding. Tracking requires its system authorization before collection and must not be incentivized or manipulated.

Choose one-time location access for suitable individual tasks using the system location button on supported platforms; preserve permitted customization and all localized/accessibility-sized text. Protect secrets with established authentication/keychain mechanisms. For Mac, account for sandboxing/distribution and fast user switching. For visionOS, separate system rendering assistance from permission-gated Full Space ARKit data; gaze remains private, and imported phone-camera assumptions may need removal or content import.

**Before → decision → after:** A bird journal asks for contacts, microphone, and continuous location at launch although only “Attach current location” uses location. Decision: request only the specific action's needed access. After, journaling works immediately; the attachment action offers the supported location control, and its purpose explains adding the sighting's location.

Deliver a data-purpose/access matrix and corrected permission sequence/copy or implementation. Fail if collection precedes required consent, copy obscures the real use, or unrelated work is gated on optional access. Report code/flow evidence separately from actual authorization prompts and privacy-setting behavior; this procedure does not certify security or legal compliance.

Use [Sign in with Apple](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-sign-in-with-apple/SKILL.md) for that authentication choice and [Augmented reality](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-augmented-reality/SKILL.md) when room/camera access is essential.

# Explain the entitlement before the purchase

Read [Apple In-App Purchase](../../references/apple-in-app-purchase.md). Inspect what is sold, entitlement duration, existing-customer paths, prices/offers, and requested design/review/adaptation. Preserve the payment stack; use current platform documentation for implementation/eligibility rather than treating this design snapshot as current commercial policy.

Classify the product first: digital goods/features/subscriptions use this model; physical goods/services and donations belong to Apple Pay guidance. Choose consumable, nonconsumable, auto-renewing, or nonrenewing behavior according to what access means. Advanced Commerce needs eligibility, not merely a large catalog.

Show usable value before prompting and keep purchase discovery integrated. Use clear short product names, complete localized billed amounts, and the unmodified system confirmation. For subscriptions, display included service, period, full billing total, any introductory/trial duration, subsequent price and automatic billing, Terms/Privacy, and sign-in/restore for existing purchasers. Keep full totals more prominent than equivalent-period breakdowns; never resell a new subscription to someone who already has access. TV should reduce entry through another device/code; Watch still needs complete terms and an easy close/cancel route.

Define what follows redemption/purchase and how people manage access. Apply entitlements promptly, support prelaunch redemption, explain eligible Family Sharing for purchaser/recipient, and make subscription management/cancellation easy to reach. Purchase help should show useful product/date context and an obvious system refund request; do not promise Apple's refund outcome.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a language app advertises “Only $2/month,” bills annually, hides restore, and shows the same offer to active subscribers. Decision: terms and existing access must be explicit. After, the paywall leads with the full annual charge and period, explains any trial-to-paid transition, exposes sign-in/restore, and routes existing subscribers to content/management instead of repurchase.

Deliver corrected offer/paywall/help states or implementation. Fail if the billed total is obscured, existing purchases cannot be recovered, trial billing is ambiguous, or cancellation/refund access is buried. Static copy review cannot establish StoreKit transactions, entitlement synchronization, eligibility, or refunds; identify sandbox/device checks still pending.

Use [Apple Pay](../apple-hig-apple-pay/SKILL.md) for physical commerce and [Writing](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-writing/SKILL.md) for precise offer/help language.

# Designing for visionOS Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-visionos) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Apple Vision Pro presents a spatial canvas containing windows, volumes, and 3D objects. Apps normally start in the Shared Space beside other apps; a person can choose a Full Space in which one app provides mixed, portal-based, or fully surrounding content. Passthrough is live camera imagery of the actual surroundings. The Digital Crown adjusts how much of that context remains visible. Spatial Audio models the room acoustically; with permission to understand surroundings an app can refine its audio experience. Eyes typically target content and an indirect hand gesture activates it; direct gestures can touch virtual content. Accessibility includes VoiceOver, Switch Control, Dwell Control, Guided Access, and Head Pointer. Standard components provide an accessible starting point; enhance custom content with the platform frameworks. Device safety matters: the source specifies use by people age 13 or older, and excludes use while operating vehicles or heavy machinery or moving around hazards such as streets, stairs, and balconies. Consult Apple’s current device user guide for operational restrictions. ## Best practices - Use space, audio, immersion, passthrough, and eye/hand inputs deliberately. Select the least immersive presentation that delivers each moment rather than making every task fully immersive. - Prefer standard windows for contained UI and ordinary tasks. People can position windows and dynamic scaling preserves readability at different distances. - Preserve visual comfort: cameras mediate both real and virtual vision. Position content relative to the head inside a comfortable field of view regardless of posture or height. - Avoid requiring head turns, body repositioning, or excessive movement during full immersion. Bring useful content to a resting person. - Avoid rapid, overwhelming, abrupt motion or motion without a stable visual reference. - Make indirect gestures work with hands resting at the sides or in the lap. # SharePlay Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/shareplay) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. SharePlay synchronizes a real-time activity across participants’ devices alongside FaceTime or Messages. Start can come from app UI, FaceTime, or a link; the system guides app installation and content/subscription access. Each participant normally needs their own entitlement to purchased/subscribed content. ## Best practices Use it for simultaneous participation; add saved state or sharing links for later asynchronous collaboration. Match the activity: synchronized identical views for watching/browsing, personal roles/views for games where useful. Adapt across platforms and communication contexts. Provide a recognizable SharePlay control or system share entry point. Bring joiners directly to shared content, using dismissible prerequisites and postponing profiles/nonessential onboarding; provisional access or Family Sharing can lower purchase friction. Invitations need concise descriptions, titles, and appropriate art. Explain who caused shared changes; system playback synchronization can pause for everyone. Use SharePlay as noun or action verb without adjectives such as spatial/virtual and without altered suffixes. ## Platform considerations No extra tvOS rules; watchOS is unsupported. ### iOS, iPadOS, macOS Support shared video continuing in Picture in Picture on phone/tablet and a usable continuing playback window on Mac while other work proceeds. ### visionOS Standard windows share by screen mirroring through the window-bar Share button; adopt SharePlay for volumes and immersive content. #### Designing shared activities Keep shared objects, windows, sounds, and interactions in a consistent relative location through shared context. Prefer a window start, because immersive-only entry needs custom sharing UI. Resolve simultaneous use naturally with predictable rules rather than UI that steals another person’s tool. Keep views/immersion coordinated except when a distinct perspective is meaningful; represent a participant in a separate immersive context with a contact image and retain FaceTime Audio. Ask before an immersion change interrupts someone’s other task. Volume/subtitle/accessibility preferences remain per-person. Offer a clear way to leave/rejoin, with a windowed continuation when possible. #### Personas Remote Vision Pro participants may appear as spatial Personas, or contact photos if no Persona exists. Other devices use 2D video windows. Nearby Vision Pro participants see one another through passthrough with content aligned in the same physical place. Offer UI alternatives for activities relying on gestures/facial expression so people without spatial Personas participate fully. #### Spatial templates Side-by-side places people on a curve facing shared media; surround seats a group around central 3D/tabletop content; conversational seats a group around a center with content at the edge, favoring social interaction/background tasks over everyone manipulating the same view. Split complex activities into stages with appropriate system/custom templates. Tie changes to explicit actions, avoid frequent or large moves, fade seat changes, and give reorientation cues. #### Custom templates Custom seats apply to spatial Personas, while others can participate without seats. Nearby real people cannot be virtually moved; use position markers when real arrangement matters. Choose seat direction rather than blindly accepting the content-center default. Plan all supported seats up front, normally five for the maximum five spatial Personas, leaving seats stable when someone leaves and adding spectators where a game limit permits. Space seats at least 1 m apart; too-close Personas become contact photos. Choose a balanced fill order for partial attendance. Keep player/spectator/team roles independent of seats except where one role truly requires a location, such as a host. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/shareplay) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: September 9, 2026, December 5, 2023, June 21, 2023, December 19, 2022.

# Privacy Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Communicate collection and usage clearly and protect granted data. Keep App Store privacy disclosures accurate for new releases and updates; people rely on them before downloading. ## Best practices Collect only what the specific feature requires and make access as precise as possible. Respect Hide My Email, Mail Privacy Protection, and tracking choices. Prefer on-device processing, including Create ML/Neural Engine where useful, to avoid unnecessary server transfers. Use system encryption, key management, and established security protections, including CloudKit’s additional encrypted data types where available. ## Requesting permission Protected categories include personal/location/health/financial/contact information, user-created content, messages/calendar/music/gameplay/HomeKit data, media, Bluetooth/Wi-Fi/local network resources, camera/microphone, the advertising identifier, and permission-gated ARKit data in a visionOS Full Space. The system displays the app’s purpose string and stores choices/descriptions in privacy settings. Ask when the person invokes the relevant feature. Request at launch only when access is essential and obviously necessary, such as location for navigation or room information for a spatial game that needs walls. Write a short, specific, active, complete sentence in sentence case with a period, explaining both use and reason. Vague promises of a better experience and commands to enable access do not explain the need. ### Pre-alert screens, windows, or views Usually context explains the request. If extra explanation is essential, use one button clearly leading to the system alert, such as Continue/Next; do not label it Allow or mimic the actual consent choice. Do not add cancellation, close, or other actions except those needed for legal consent. These restrictions apply to pre-permission custom explanations, not ordinary unrelated onboarding screens. ### Tracking requests Show the AppTrackingTransparency alert before collecting tracking information, including if tracking begins at launch. Do not offer incentives, imitate a permission prompt, display an image of the alert, annotate behind it, or otherwise manipulate rushed choices. Such patterns can cause App Review rejection. A legally required consent view before/after the system alert is permitted by the source’s stated review guidance. ## Location button On iOS/iPadOS/watchOS, the system location button provides one-time access at the task’s moment of need. The first tap teaches and confirms its behavior through a system alert; later taps grant access without repeating that education. Authorization expires when app use ends. With no prior status it resembles Allow Once; an existing While Using status is unchanged. Use it for individual tasks such as attaching a location or finding a nearby item/store. Customize only the supplied title, filled/outline glyph, foreground/background colors, and corner radius. Keep all localized and accessibility-size text untruncated and maintain contrast/transparency limits. Persistent customization violations can prevent location access even though the button still triggers other app actions. ## Protecting data Prefer passkeys; if passwords remain, add two-factor verification. Use Face ID, Optic ID, or Touch ID to protect continued signed-in access where appropriate. Store secrets in the encrypted keychain, never plaintext files even with restrictive permissions. Prefer established authentication, Sign in with Apple, and Password AutoFill over invented schemes. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS/tvOS/watchOS rules are listed. ### macOS Sign externally distributed apps with a valid Developer ID. Use sandboxing to limit resource/data access; Mac App Store apps require it. Account for fast user switching rather than assuming the current person is the only signed-in account. ### visionOS System ARKit algorithms support lighting, mapping, persistence, segmentation, and related rendering in Shared Space without exposing raw data to apps. ARKit API access requires Full Space, and plane estimation, scene reconstruction, image anchoring, and hand tracking require permission. Gaze remains private: system hover feedback can respond before a tap without disclosing where someone looks. Compatibility back-camera input is blank; front-camera input represents spatial Personas with permission. Adapt imported phone/tablet camera-dependent features by removal or content import instead of assuming conventional camera capture. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 21, 2023.

# Apple In-App Purchase Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/apple-in-app-purchase) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Use In-App Purchase for digital goods, premium features, and digital subscriptions. Apple Pay serves physical goods/services and donations. Consumables deplete and can be rebought; nonconsumables do not expire; auto-renewables continue until canceled; nonrenewing subscriptions require a new purchase to extend time. Advanced Commerce API serves qualifying complex, frequently updated/multicreator catalogs and bundled subscription add-ons; consult eligibility and review rules. ## Best practices Let people experience value before purchase, keeping shopping integrated with app styling. Use short clear names/descriptions and always show the complete billed price. Show a usable store only where payments are allowed, explaining parental/payment restrictions if needed. Use the system confirmation sheet without imitation or modification. ### Supporting Family Sharing Eligible nonconsumables/auto-renewables can be shared with up to five additional family members across devices. Highlight sharing in product names/signup information, explain benefits and the system’s notifications/settings, and tailor copy for both the purchaser and family recipients. ### Providing help Offer missing-purchase help, FAQs, support/feedback, contextual product/date information, and alternatives such as immediate fulfillment, while keeping a clearly labeled refund request readily visible without extra scrolling/screens. Hand off to the system refund flow; do not speculate about Apple’s approval or refund policies. A help link to Apple’s refund explanation is appropriate. ## Auto-renewable subscriptions Explain benefits and terms during onboarding with a clear action. Offer suitable content tiers/durations and sampling via freemium access, metering, or trials. Prompt at meaningful moments and make subscribing generally findable. Do not advertise a new subscription to an existing subscriber; let cross-app/web customers sign in instead of paying again. ### Making signup effortless Give distinct short option names, price/duration, introductory price and period, and subsequent standard price. Ask only essential initial data. On tvOS, use another device/code for entry/authentication. Signup must include subscription name, period, included service/content, localized complete billing amount, sign-in/restore for existing purchasers, and Terms/Privacy links. Put full billing totals above equivalent-period price breakdowns. Clearly state trial length and automatic billing after it. Include signup in settings. ### Supporting offer codes One-time codes from App Store Connect work through redemption links, supported in-app UI, or App Store entry; choose these for restricted/small distributions. Custom reusable codes fit mass campaigns and redeem by URL or supported in-app UI, not App Store account settings. Custom codes use ASCII letters/numbers only. Explain offer terms and redemption clearly. A Redeem Code action should open the system flow; it can appear in paywalls, onboarding, or settings. Optional promotional art replaces the default app icon. Apply unlocked entitlements immediately and welcome people appropriately, including those who redeemed before first launch. ### Helping people manage their subscriptions Show subscription summaries and upcoming renewal near account/settings management. Prefer system subscription UI for upgrade/downgrade/cancel. Relevant alternative plans, discounts, or later win-back offers can help, but cancellation must remain easy to identify and reach. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS/visionOS rules. ### watchOS Include the same required subscription information while explicitly describing device-specific content/function differences. A modal sheet can present the complete details with a convenient Close; custom flows also need Close/Cancel to free content. Make duration/discount comparisons compact, either separate purchase buttons locked to descriptions or a list plus a clearly labeled purchase button reflecting the chosen option. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/apple-in-app-purchase) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: September 17, 2026, September 12, 2023, November 3, 2022.

# Interrupt only for a decision that warrants it

Read [the alert guide](../../references/alerts.md). Apply the following as application advice and preserve the documented deliberate-destruction exception.

Inspect the triggering condition, urgency, reversibility, prior user intent, platform, and create/review/adapt request. Establish whether immediate attention is necessary. Do not turn every status update or startup network failure into an alert; ordinary undoable deletion can use recovery instead. Record evidence of the actual outcome and default-key behavior, not just button color.

Write a contextual neutral title and only useful supporting text; name outcomes instead of Yes/No. Use at most three buttons with meaningful roles and a safe Cancel beside destruction. Distinguish unexpected destructive consequences from confirmation of explicitly requested destruction: the latter may retain a normal default so Return confirms intent. Cancel is not the default; consider no default when deliberate reading is necessary. A single default completion acknowledgment should be Done, while OK can acknowledge purely informational content. Do not impose one platform's button geometry everywhere.

Implement the alert/handlers or deliver exact copy, role/default/order, trigger, and result specification; reviews must identify the specific misleading consequence or unnecessary interruption. Use fields only when resolution requires input and secure entry for passwords. Apply relevant platform accessory/cancellation rules: Mac suppression/Help only when useful, visionOS accessory limits and parent/space relationship, keyboard/remote alternate cancellation where supported. Post-action alternatives may belong in an action sheet.

**Worked transformation:** Before: an editor displays `Error 47` with OK/Cancel after an unrequested operation would overwrite unsaved work; Return commits overwrite. Decision: the consequence is unexpected and concealed. After: explain the conflicting draft, offer explicit safe recovery/cancellation and appropriately destructive replacement, and define a default that cannot accidentally accept unexplained loss.

Deliver the artifact and trigger/outcome/default contract. Verify Return, Cancel, supported escape, enlarged text, and repeated errors without stacked alerts. Fail for concealed loss, misleading action text, no safe cancellation, or routine status forcing interruption. Separate handler checks from native alert/assistive execution.

Use [action-sheets](../apple-hig-action-sheets/SKILL.md) for alternatives, [undo-and-redo](../../../apple-hig-patterns/.topics/apple-hig-undo-and-redo/SKILL.md) for reversible work, or [modality](../../../apple-hig-patterns/.topics/apple-hig-modality/SKILL.md) for surrounding exits.

# Alerts Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/alerts) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. An alert interrupts to communicate urgent, critical information and useful actions, including problems, unexpected data loss, or important confirmations. ## Best practices Reserve alerts for situations that warrant immediate attention. Put informational status in context when no action is required. Common undoable deletions generally need no confirmation; uncommon irreversible destruction does. Avoid startup alerts: cached or placeholder content with a discreet problem explanation is often a better response to an unavailable network. ## Anatomy Alerts are modal and adapt their appearance to iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS rather than using one universal layout. ## Content Use a title, optional message, and up to three buttons. iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS can include text fields; macOS and visionOS can include an icon and accessory view. macOS additionally supports a suppression checkbox and Help button. Use direct, neutral, approachable wording without blaming the person or concealing severity. The title should explain what happened, its context, and cause as concisely as possible, generally within two lines. Avoid a bare error label or code. Complete-sentence titles use sentence case and punctuation; fragments use title case without punctuation. Additional text should add information in brief complete sentences. Clear action labels should make button explanations unnecessary; if instructions are unavoidable, use device-neutral language such as choose and the exact title without quotation marks. Include an input field only when resolving the situation requires it, with secure entry for passwords. ## Buttons Use short, usually one- or two-word, title-case action labels without punctuation. Prefer specific outcomes over Yes/No or ambiguous OK; reserve OK for purely informational acknowledgment. A cancellation action is always Cancel. Place the expected/default action at the trailing end of a row or top of a stack, with cancellation generally leading or at the bottom. Apply destructive styling to destructive consequences the person did not deliberately request. A confirmation of an explicitly chosen destruction, such as Empty Trash, can retain a normal default action so Return confirms intent. Always provide Cancel alongside destructive actions, but do not make Cancel the default. To force a deliberate reading, consider no default. A single default acknowledgment button should be Done rather than Cancel. Support familiar alternate cancellation where appropriate: Home Screen exit on iOS/iPadOS; Escape or Command-Period on attached keyboards in iOS/iPadOS/macOS/visionOS; Menu on the tvOS remote. ## Platform considerations No additional tvOS or watchOS rules are specified. ### iOS, iPadOS Use action sheets for multiple choices following an intentional action. Keep titles and optional messages short to minimize scrolling, while accommodating enlarged accessibility text. ### macOS The app icon appears automatically but can be replaced. Repeating alerts can offer suppression; necessary details can use an accessory view, and Help can open documentation. Reserve a caution symbol for situations needing extra attention, particularly unexpected loss, rather than routine overwrite, save, or empty-trash tasks. ### visionOS In Shared Space, an alert sits slightly in front of its parent window and stays attached when the window moves. In Full Space, it centers in the wearer's field of view. An accessory view must be no taller than 154 pt and use a 16-pt corner radius. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Modality](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/modality) [Action sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/action-sheets) [Sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sheets) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: February 2, 2024, September 12, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# Apple HIG: End-to-end behavior and recovery

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Trace the person’s task from entry through completion, cancellation, interruption and recovery. Select the pattern procedure for the actual failure or desired behavior before selecting its controls.
2. Preserve the current work, selection and navigation context across the transitions that matter. Choose interruption or modality according to urgency and task scope, not visual emphasis.
3. For asynchronous or recurring work, separate current progress, eventual result, error recovery and unavailable capability. For audio/video/haptics, specify user control and environmental behavior.
4. Deliver a transition/state specification, a correction to the supplied flow, or ranked findings tied to observed steps. Test alternate exits and resumption, not just the success path.

# Resolve modality as a task contract

Read [the modality guide](../../references/modality.md). Use its platform facts as constraints; the decision process below is application advice. A large or fullscreen presentation does not by itself prove modality: establish whether the parent is blocked and what ends that mode.

## Inspect the interruption

Determine create, review, or adaptation mode from the request. Inspect the supplied flows, screens, implementation, or brief for the initiating action, parent context, reason to interrupt, task length, side navigation, and retained work. Identify the platform and whether the task must coexist with another document, window, or reference view. Record what is actually known: a screenshot cannot prove that the background is interactive or that dismissal discards data.

Describe the task in one outcome sentence and identify why normal navigation or an in-context control would be insufficient. If blocking the parent brings no clear decision/focus benefit, revise toward an in-context or nonmodal presentation. Do not preserve modality merely because the current mockup uses a dimmed background.

## Choose presentation and completion together

1. Separate urgent critical information, a scoped related task, an intentional choice, and substantial editing/immersion. Route urgent critical information to alerts, choices to action-sheets/confirmation-dialog guidance, and a short task attached to a parent to sheets or a suitable popover. A fullscreen editor can support substantial work without being modal; document blocking behavior explicitly.
2. Choose a platform-supported candidate and load that topic before prescribing its detailed interaction. A separate window can preserve parallel work on iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS. A popover must not be carried onto an unsupported platform or forced into a compact layout. A sheet's modality itself varies: iOS/iPadOS can support nonmodal sheets; Mac sheets block their parent while other app windows remain usable. For visionOS, distinguish a Shared Space presentation filling a window from Full Space immersion.
3. Keep a modal task narrow enough that the suspended parent remains understandable. If the flow has essential subviews, give it one understandable route and distinguish Back from exiting the task. If it becomes a miniature app with unrelated navigation, split work into ordinary navigation, a separate window, or another appropriate nonmodal workspace instead of adding layers of modal navigation.
4. Specify every available exit against the same data policy: explicit completion, Cancel/Close, interactive dismissal, platform keyboard/remote escape where supported, and any product-defined navigation away. For each exit state whether changes are committed, retained as a draft, discarded after a deliberate decision, or preserved while dismissal is cancelled. Protect created work regardless of whether the exit began with a gesture or a button. Ask about persistence only if the product contract cannot be inferred; otherwise state a reversible assumption and implement it consistently.
5. Name the task and exits so the person can predict the result. Provide a familiar visible exit, using the platform's placement conventions from the selected presentation topic. “Back” changes steps; it must not silently abandon the whole task. Keep relevant guidance close to the work rather than making a title carry instructions.
6. Resolve competing presentations. Dismiss one modal before presenting its replacement and retain only needed context. An alert may appear above modal content for a necessary decision; do not stack alerts. Define which view returns after the alert or replacement so a save/discard decision cannot strand the person or resurrect obsolete content.

Perform the requested action: implement the presentation/exit behavior in the supplied code, create a flow and state specification when designing, or produce a prioritized review grounded in identifiable transitions. Adaptation must revise the presentation and exit contract for the destination platform, not just rename a sheet.

## Deliver and verify

Provide the changed artifact plus a concise transition contract: entry → parent availability → task steps → completion → each dismissal path → resulting data and return destination. In a review, give the observed evidence, consequence, and concrete repair for each issue; list unseen behavior as an inspection question, not a defect.

Exercise or trace a clean exit and an exit after making an edit. Verify that button, gesture, and supported escape paths agree on data protection; Back preserves the task; completion updates the intended parent; reopening does not restore an obsolete transient view; and no second sheet or alert traps the flow. Inspect focus transfer and restoration in code and exercise them when a suitable runtime exists. Fail the design if there is no discoverable exit, unfinished work disappears through one route, a critical decision can be bypassed accidentally, or background blocking contradicts the task contract. Report native input, assistive technology, and Apple-device behavior as unverified when only static or Linux checks were possible.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** A tablet archive app opens “Add Collection” as a sheet. Choosing a cover presents another sheet; a downward swipe from either screen loses the entered title. A top `Back` on the first screen dismisses everything.

**Decision:** Creating a collection is a narrow related task, but cover selection belongs within it. Dismissal and back-navigation need distinct contracts; every dismissal path must protect the edited title.

**After:** Keep one collection sheet with an internal cover-selection step. The first step has `Cancel` and `Done`; the cover step has `Back` returning with its choice. Specify a shared exit handler: clean dismissal closes; edited dismissal offers keep editing or the product's explicit save/discard resolution. Completion creates one collection and returns to the archive. Verify that the swipe and Cancel paths invoke the same protection and that Back never destroys the draft. This proposed flow is application advice, not an observation of an existing app.

## Conditional handoffs

Load sheets, alerts, popovers, action-sheets, panels, or windows only for the selected presentation's detailed rules. Use entering-data or undo-and-redo when persistence/recovery is the real problem; use accessibility when focus boundaries and exit discoverability need deeper treatment. Carry the transition contract into that work.

# Modality Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/modality) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A modal mode blocks its parent until explicitly dismissed. It can deliver critical information, clarify a recent action, support a narrow task, or focus attention on an immersive/complex activity. Alerts are available across platforms, while activity views, sheets, and confirmation dialogs or action sheets provide context-specific options. For a distinct task, iOS, iPadOS, and macOS commonly use a sheet or popover; iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS can also use a separate window. Fullscreen experiences can also be nonmodal. ## Best practices Use modality only for a clear focus/decision benefit. Keep tasks brief and direct so the suspended context remains memorable. Avoid a miniature app inside the modal; if subviews are essential, offer one understandable route and distinguish back-navigation from dismissal. A fullscreen modal can suit substantial editing, camera, or media; in visionOS Shared Space it fills a window, while Full Space can create immersion. Provide an obvious familiar exit: often a top control or downward swipe on iOS/iPadOS/watch, or a body control on Mac/tvOS. Before losing created content through either gesture or button, explain consequences and offer appropriate save/discard choices. Identify the task with a clear title and necessary guidance. Dismiss one modal before showing another, keeping only the necessary context; an alert can appear over other modal content, but never stack multiple alerts. ## Platform considerations The source adds no separate rules for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, or watchOS. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sheets) [Alerts](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/alerts) [Popovers](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/popovers) [Action sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/action-sheets) [Activity views](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/activity-views) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: December 5, 2023, June 21, 2023.
